# 21 — TwinCAT PLC Library Compatibility Plan

> **Status:** planning document. This file is the complete
> recursive catalog of every function, function block, method,
> property, and event documented in the Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 PLC
> library manuals, together with a per-library analysis of what
> TetherPLC must provide for each API to exist.

---

## 1. Purpose and scope

TwinCAT users have ~9,900 documented PLC-callable APIs spread over
108 product manuals. This plan answers two questions for each of
them:

1. **What is the API?** — name, kind, recursive documentation
   path, parameters with types and descriptions, return values,
   and behavioral description, sufficient to implement and
   document a compatible TetherPLC function.
2. **How does it tie into TetherPLC?** — which tier of TetherPLC
   infrastructure it maps onto, and — when it interfaces with
   facilities the runtime cannot currently reach (serial ports,
   sockets, ADS routers, databases, motion axes, vision engines)
   — exactly what must be built to support it.

## 2. Sources and method

- **Source corpus:** the Beckhoff InfoSys "TwinCAT 3 PLC libraries"
  overview (`infosys.beckhoff.com`, page 4340797963) and every
  linked English product manual: **108 PDFs, ~654 MB, ~1.15 M
  extracted text lines**.
- **Extraction:** each PDF was text-extracted and parsed for
  numbered section headings, `FUNCTION` / `FUNCTION_BLOCK` /
  `METHOD` / `PROPERTY` / `EVENT` declarations, `VAR_INPUT` /
  `VAR_OUTPUT` / `VAR_IN_OUT` / `VAR_TEMP` blocks, and the newer
  "Inputs / Outputs / Arguments" parameter tables.
- **Result:** **9,947 API entries** across 107 of 108 manuals,
  each carrying its recursive section path (`cat`), section
  number (`§`), kind, parameters, and description where the
  manual provides one.
- **Honest limitations:** a small number of entries are prose
  sub-headings that carry partial signatures; manuals that are
  conceptual rather than API references (notably the Advanced
  Motion Pack overview, `TF5400`) yield few or no entries —
  this is a documentation-format limitation, not proof of
  absence. Some entries are documented procedure/tool
  parameter sets (mxAutomation motion commands, Vision tool
  configurations) rather than `FUNCTION` declarations; they
  are retained because they are part of the callable surface.
  Beckhoff licenses several libraries (mxAutomation,
  uniVAL, Vision engine internals); entries are catalogued but
  implementation may require a licensed engine or an explicit
  "unsupported" declaration.

## 3. Compatibility tiers

Every library is classified by the deepest TetherPLC layer it
needs. A library only ships when every API in it reaches its
required tier.

| Tier | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **T0 — Pure IEC** | Implementable entirely in the compatibility library (ST or native kernels). No runtime services. | Tc2_Standard, Tc2_Math, Tc3_Filter, Tc3_PackML |
| **T1 — Runtime service** | Needs a new `TplcServices` hook, image feature, task feature, or debug-plane extension. | Tc2_System (ADS, task stats), Tc3_DynamicMemory, Tc3_EventLogger, Tc3_Module |
| **T2 — Host OS adapter** | Needs OS facilities the runtime does not touch: serial ports, TCP/UDP sockets + multicast, filesystem, databases, fieldbuses, TLS. | Tc2_SerialCom, Tc2_TcpIp, Tc2_ModbusRTU, all Building protocols, Tc3_sACN |
| **T3 — Motion backend** | Needs an axis/NC/motion engine: trajectory generation, PLCopen state machines, camming, kinematics. | All Tc2_MC2/NCI/NC, Tc3_MC3, hydraulics, drives |
| **T4 — External engine / licensed** | Needs an engine that does not exist in TetherPLC and may be licensed/proprietary: vision, ML, analytics storage, speech, robotics. | Tc3_vision, Tc3_MLL, Tc3_mxAutomation, Tc3_Speech |

### 3.1 What TetherPLC already provides

- **Compilation:** ST and FBD frontends → MIR → LLVM host `.so`,
  ARM `ET_REL`, or TPLB PIC blob. A compatibility library can be
  shipped as ordinary ST sources or as a precompiled package.
- **Runtime:** deterministic task scheduler, process image
  (`%I/%Q/%M`), retain storage, events, diagnostics, watchdog,
  shadow-run candidates, online change with migration.
- **Services:** `TplcServices` callback table (logging,
  diagnostics, steady time, retain dirty, event raise, generic
  service lookup) — the extension point for every T1/T2 need.
- **Debug plane:** watch/force/write, suspend/step, trace,
  symbol resolve — the natural host for monitoring-style APIs.

### 3.2 What TetherPLC cannot currently access

None of the following exist in the runtime today. Each is a
prerequisite for the libraries noted:

| Missing facility | Needed by | Implementation sketch |
|---|---|---|
| **Serial/UART ports** | Tc2_SerialCom, Modbus RTU, DALI, DMX, M-Bus, RFID, UPS, GSM/SMS, most Building buses | `tplc-serial` service: termios on host, UART+DMA on MCU; byte-stream + RS485 direction control; deterministic write deadlines |
| **TCP/UDP sockets + multicast** | Tc2_TcpIp, sACN, BACnet, S7, EtherNet/IP, OPC UA, MQTT/IoT, FTP, PJLink, RRCS, IEC 60870-5-104 | `tplc-net` service: non-blocking socket pool, DNS, multicast join/leave; all protocol codecs live in compat libraries above it |
| **ADS/AMS router** | Tc2_System ADS blocks, Tc2_Coupler, Tc2_DataExchange | `tplc-ads` service: AMS/TCP transport, symbol lookup, read/write/state requests; or native named-variable service |
| **Filesystem** | Tc3_JsonXml persistence, Tc2_Utilities file helpers, data loggers | `tplc-fs` service: sandboxed read/write, or map to host FS with path policy |
| **Database drivers** | Tc2/Tc3_Database, Analytics storage | `tplc-db` service: ODBC/SQLite-class driver pool |
| **EtherCAT master hooks** | Tc3_EtherCATDiag, Tc2_EtherCAT, Tc3_EtherCATExtSync | Control-plane bridge to the EtherCAT master (sibling `Tether` repo has master/slave/PDO machinery): AL-state query, SII access, PDO/domain introspection, DC sync status |
| **Axis/NC motion engine** | All Motion libraries (~40 manuals, ~2,000+ APIs) | `tplc-motion` service: axis objects (position/velocity/torque), PLCopen MC state machines, interpolation (lin/circ/helix/spline), cam tables, homing, gear/coupling, handshakes; deterministic cycle-budgeted |
| **Vision engine** | Tc3_vision | External engine (GPU/CPU) + image-buffer service; camera acquisition via GenICam/Ethernet Vision or frame-grabber driver |
| **ML inference** | Tc3_MLL, Tc3_MlServer | ONNX/TFLite-class runtime or licensed engine; tensor buffers via service |
| **Analytics/time-series** | Tc3_Analytics* | Aggregation + storage services; can start as ring-buffer + exporter |
| **Speech** | Tc3_Speech | ASR/TTS engine (external process or library) |
| **Robotics engines** | Tc3_mxAutomation, Tc3_uniValPlc | Licensed Beckhoff engines; likely permanent "unsupported" unless a license/SDK is obtained |
| **Proprietary/licensed protocols** | mxAutomation, uniVAL, some Building/vision internals | Specification may be unpublished; catalogued APIs may be implementable only to stub depth |

## 4. Architecture: how the catalog maps onto TetherPLC

Compatibility is layered, mirroring how TwinCAT itself layers
libraries over the real-time kernel:

```
TwinCAT ST/FBD application
        │  (source-compatible or binary-compatible)
┌───────▼────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ TetherPLC compat libraries (per Tc2_*/Tc3_* product) │
│  T0 pure-IEC impls · type definitions · enums        │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Service layer (new TplcServices / host daemons)      │
│  net · serial · ads · fs · db · ethercat · motion   │
│  vision · ml · analytics · speech                   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ TetherPLC runtime: tasks, image, retain, events,     │
│ diagnostics, shadow run, debug plane, TPLB blobs    │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Key design rules:

- **Determinism:** every service call from a task context must be
  bounded or asynchronous. Blocking serial/socket I/O inside a
  scan cycle is forbidden; protocol FBs use the TwinCAT pattern
  of state-machine blocks fed by background transport services.
  TetherPLC's existing event/diagnostic services are the model.
- **Package model:** each TwinCAT product maps to a TetherPLC
  package (`tplc` manifest) declaring its service dependencies,
  so a project only pulls in `tc2-serialcom` if it uses it.
- **Type system:** TwinCAT types (`AXIS_REF`, `E_*`, `ST_*`,
  enumerations) are declared in per-library `.st`/`.duts`-style
  sources inside the compat package; the catalog below lists
  every parameter type needed.
- **Host vs MCU:** T0/T1 libraries compile to both host `.so`
  and TPLB blobs. T2/T3/T4 services are host-side (or external
  MCU peripherals); the MCU path gets stubs that fault cleanly
  with a documented error code.

## 7. Complete recursive API catalog

Every entry below was extracted from the named Beckhoff manual.
`§` is the manual section number; the path in parentheses is
the recursive category ancestry. Entries are grouped by manual
in overview order. Parameter tables preserve the manual's own
descriptions; "—" means the manual gave a name/type but no
per-parameter prose.

### Tc2_Coupler — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_Coupler_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_Coupler_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 6
- **Status:** bus-coupler (BKxxxx) configuration is host-IO domain — no PLC-side FBs needed; documented gap
- **Integration:** Mailbox coupling between images needs an ADS-like transport.

#### Function blocks

##### `ReadWriteTerminalReg` — §3.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `STATE` | `BYTE` | Status byte of the terminal channel. |
| `DATAIN` | `WORD` | Data input word of the terminal channel. |
| `REGNO` | `BYTE` | Number of the register to read or write. |
| `READ` | `BOOL` | A positive edge at this input activates the function block, |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Function blocks` | `` | — |
| `CTRL` | `BYTE` | Control byte of the terminal channel. |
| `DATAOUT` | `WORD` | Data output word of the terminal channel. |
| `BUSY` | `BOOL` | When the function block is activated, this output is set and |

**Description:** The function block ReadWriteTerminalReg enables convenient access to the terminal's registers via the control/status byte of the terminal channel (register communication). In the standard operation mode, the data inputs and outputs of the intelligent terminals (e.g. an analog output terminal) are used to exchange the analog output data. A handshake via the control/status byte permits register access. The data input and output variables are used here to transfer the register values. A positive edge at the READ or WRITE input causes the register with number REGNO to be read or written to. Write protection of the register is disabled by the function block for a write access and enabled once more afterwards. With a write access to a register, the new register value is written first and then read. The value read is available at the output CURRREGVALUE. If changes made to the register values are to be stored permanently, the power supply to the coupler must be interrupted. The variables STATE, DATAIN, CTRL and DATAOUT must be linked in the TwinCAT System Manager to the corresponding I/O variables in the terminal channel.

##### `CouplerReset` — §3.2

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `STATE` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Status word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `START` | `BOOL` | The function block is enabled by a positive edge at this |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Function blocks` | `` | — |
| `CONTROL` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Control word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `BUSY` | `BOOL` | When the function block is activated, this output is set and |

**Description:** The function block CouplerReset can be used to execute a reset of the coupler via the 2-byte PLC interface. During a coupler reset, for example, the current terminal configuration is read in again by the coupler via the K-bus (terminal bus) and communication on the K-bus is reinitialized. Existing K-bus error messages for the coupler are reset. The STATE and CONTROL variables are used to perform a handshake with the coupler during the execution of the function block. These variables must therefore be linked to the Control/Status variables of the 2-byte PLC interface in the TwinCAT System Manager.

##### `FB_ReadCouplerDiag` — §3.3

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stState` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Status word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `bExecute` | `BOOL` | The function block is enabled by a positive edge at this |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stCtrl` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Control word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | When the function block is activated, this output is set and |

**Description:** The function block FB_ReadCouplerDiag allows reading of the first and second flashing sequences of the error LED on the coupler when a terminal bus or coupler error occurs. The data is transferred to the PLC via the 2-byte PLC interface. This only works if communication is maintained via the fieldbus. It must be possible to transfer data from the coupler to the PLC via the fieldbus without errors. To detect a coupler error that has occurred, the status byte of the coupler can be queried cyclically in the PLC and the function block is activated if an error occurs.

##### `FB_ReadCouplerRegs` — §3.4

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stState` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Status word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `nTerminal` | `BYTE` | Terminal number whose table register is to be accessed. |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `14 Function blocks` | `` | — |
| `stCtrl` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Control word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | When the function block is activated, this output is set and |

**Description:** This function block FB_ReadCouplerRegs provides read access to the table register in the coupler and the registers of the intelligent terminals. The coupler itself is referred to as terminal 0 (null). All the other terminals in the terminal block, with the exception of passive terminals (such as power supply terminals), are counted in ascending sequence (beginning with 1). All registers or only a subrange (between nStartReg and nEndReg) can be read. Several seconds are required to read all registers (0.255) of a coupler table. Register values that have been successfully read are found in the structure stCouplerTable. The structure is an array of high and low bytes. Each array element corresponds to a register value (e.g.: stCouplerTable[ 5 ] == Register 5).

##### `FB_WriteCouplerRegs` — §3.5

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Function blocks` | `` | — |
| `stState` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Status word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `nTerminal` | `BYTE` | Terminal number whose table register is to be accessed. |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `stCtrl` | `PLCINTFSTRUCT [} 18]` | Control word of the 2-byte PLC interface. |
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | When the function block is activated, this output is set and |

**Description:** The function block FB_WriteCouplerRegs can be used for write access to the coupler's table registers and the registers of the intelligent terminals. The coupler itself is referred to as terminal 0 (null). All the other terminals in the terminal block, with the exception of passive terminals (such as power supply terminals), are counted in ascending sequence (beginning with 1). All registers or only a subrange (between nStartReg and nEndReg) can be written to. Several seconds are required to write all registers (0.255) of a coupler table. The register values to be written are located in the structure stCouplerTable. The structure is an array of high and low bytes. Each array element corresponds to a register value (e.g.: stCouplerTable[ 5 ] == Register 5).

### Tc2_DataExchange — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_DataExchange_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_DataExchange_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 10
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED (local by-name)** — `compat/tc2/tc2_dataexchange.st`
  over the `tplc-sym` service: packages now export a variable
  table (`tplc_get_vars`) and `FB_Sym` reads/writes program
  variables by name against the live state blob.
  `FB_ReadAdsSymByName`/`FB_WriteAdsSymByName`, the six
  `...OnDelta` writers, and `FB_CheckWatchdog`/`FB_WriteWatchdog`.
  Documented difference: names address the local program (no AMS
  routing — sNetId is accepted and ignored).  Ctest
  `tc2_dataexchange_io`.
- **Integration:** Symbolic data exchange needs a named-variable transport (ADS-compatible or native).

### Tc2_EtherCAT — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_EtherCAT_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_EtherCAT_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 97
- **Status:** EtherCAT master/stack lives in Tether (io/ethercat domain); the PLC diag-read surface is delivered via `tplc-ecdiag` (Tc3_EtherCATDiag, see its entry); mailbox/state FBs (`FB_EcPhysicalReadCmd` etc.) remain unimplemented pending a master control-plane bridge
- **Integration:** EtherCAT mailbox/state access needs master service hooks.

#### EtherCAT Commands

##### `FB_EcPhysicalReadCmd` — §3.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sNetId` | `T_AmsNetId` | String containing the AMS network ID of the EtherCAT master |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | This output is set when the function block is activated, and remains set until a |

**Description:** The function block FB_EcPhysicalReadCmd can be used to send an EtherCAT read command (FPRD, APRD, BRD) to a particular EtherCAT slave or to all EtherCAT slaves. This command can be used by the PLC to read a register or the DPRAM of the EtherCAT slave controller.

##### `FB_EcPhysicalWriteCmd` — §3.2

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sNetId` | `T_AmsNetId` | String containing the AMS network ID of the EtherCAT master |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | This output is set when the function block is activated, and remains set until a |

**Description:** The function block FB_EcPhysicalWriteCmd can be used to send an EtherCAT write command (FPWR, APWR, BWR) to a particular EtherCAT slave or to all EtherCAT slaves. This command can be used by the PLC to write to a register or the DPRAM of the EtherCAT slave controller.

##### `FB_EcLogicalReadCmd` — §3.3

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sNetId` | `T_AmsNetId` | String containing the AMS network ID of the EtherCAT |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bBusy` | `BOOL` | This output is set when the function block is activated, and remains set until a |

**Description:** The master sends a logical EtherCAT write command (LRD) with the function block FB_EcLogicalReadCmd. In each slave, local address ranges (DPRAM) can be mapped to global logical address ranges. This command therefore addresses all EtherCAT slaves, which have mapping configured for the selected logical address range.

#### EtherCAT Diagnostic

##### `FB_EcGetAllMasters` — §4.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |

**Description:** The function block FB_EcMasterFrameStatistic can be used to read the frame statistics of the EtherCAT master. A distinction is made between cyclic and acyclic (queued) frames. Acyclic frames are used for the initialization or for parameter access to EtherCAT slaves. Frames are regarded as lost if they fail to return to the master or are invalid. The number of lost frames (i.e. lost or invalid cyclic frames), the number of cyclic frames per second, the number of lost queued frames (i.e. lost or invalid acyclic frames) and the number of queued frames per second is provided at the function block output.

### Tc2_IoFunctions — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_IoFunctions_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_IoFunctions_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 81
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED (general FBs) / gap (device profiles)** —
  `compat/tc2/tc2_iofunctions.st`: `IOF_GetBoxCount`,
  `IOF_GetBoxNameByAddr`, `IOF_GetBoxAddrByName(Ex)`,
  `IOF_GetDeviceCount`, `IOF_GetDeviceName`,
  `IOF_GetDeviceNetId/IDByName/IDs/InfoByName` over the package
  variable table (a "box" is an AT-bound variable; one local
  device).  `IOF_DeviceReset` reports a documented unsupported
  error — resets belong to the I/O plane (Tether).  The EtherCAT
  device-profile families (ASi, Profibus DPV1, Lightbus,
  CANopen, RAID, UPS) need the fieldbus master and stay gaps.
  Ctest `tc2_iofunctions_io`.
- **Integration:** EtherCAT device libraries (KL terminals, ASI, DPV1, IO-Link, SCIT, TcTouch, AX2000): need EtherCAT master integration and device profiles; only small helper FBs are T0.

### Tc2_MDP — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_MDP_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T1
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_MDP_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 17
- **Status:** measurement-device protocol — no public spec; documented gap
- **Integration:** Media/device parameter handling needs a device-parameter service.

**Description:** The function block FB_C69xxSetLedColor can be used to switch the user LED on the C69xx PC. The LED color is switched via a rising edge at bExecute and the eNewColor parameter. The LED can be switched off (eNewColor = eULED_Off) or set to red (eNewColor = eULED_Red), blue (eNewColor = eULED_Blue) or green (eNewColor = eULED_Green). TYPE E_UserLED_Color : ( eULED_Off := 0, eULED_Red := 1, eULED_Blue := 2, eULED_Green := 3 ); END_TYPE

- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_Utilities_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 325

### Tc3_DynamicMemory — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_DynamicMemory_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T1
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_DynamicMemory_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 2
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED** — `compat/tc3/tc3_dynmem.st` over the
  `tplc-dynmem` bounded-arena host service (64 blocks / 64 KiB max
  / 1 MiB arena, deterministic, no host heap).  Handles are
  integer ids (no POINTER semantics — documented difference);
  METHOD calls are edge-triggered `nCmd` inputs.  Ctest
  `tc3_dynmem_io`.
- **Integration:** Dynamic allocation needs a heap/arena service in the runtime; deterministic sizing rules required.

### Tc3_EtherCATDiag — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_EtherCATDiag_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_EtherCATDiag_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 2
- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED (sim contract) — `tplc-ecdiag` host service reads the `ec.coediag.*` params over Tether IO (`TPLC_EC_IO`, falls back to `TPLC_MOTION_IO`): `ec.coediag.slave` selects the port address, `ec.coediag.history` returns the 0x10F3 header + 22-byte ETG.1020 records, `ec.coediag.ack` writes newest-acked. `compat/tc3/tc3_ecdiag.st` provides `FB_CoE_DiagHistory_Read` over the `FB_EcDiagRead` builtin; entries surface as flattened parallel `aE*` member arrays (no user STRUCTs in this dialect), `sMsgText` is a generated `TID=/CODE=` fallback (ESI/XML texts unavailable), `tReadInterval` maps to `nReadIntervalScans`, and `diag_code_type` is approximated. `tc3_ecdiag_io` e2e green against `tether_io_motion_server --clock sim` (read/ack/slave counts). Remaining: real-master hookup needs per-slave CoE SDO 0x10F3 reads bridged into the same params; `FB_CoE_DiagHistory_ReadAxis` needs Tc2_MC2 `AXIS_REF` objects; ESI text lookup and module/profile diag-code typing unsupported.
- **Integration:** EtherCAT diagnostics need master control-plane hooks (AL state, SII, PDO config). Tether (sibling repo) has an EtherCAT master; bridging is cross-repo work.

### Tc3_EventLogger — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_EventLogger_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T1
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_EventLogger_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 146
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED (core + aggregate surface)** —
  `compat/tc3/tc3_eventlog.st` over the `tplc-eventlog` bounded
  journal (128 entries, raise/clear/confirm lifecycle).
  `FB_TcEvent`/`FB_TcMessage`/`FB_TcAlarm`/`FB_TcEventQuery` plus the
  aggregate `FB_TcEventLogger` (filtered clear/confirm alarms,
  clear-all/confirm-all, IsAlarmRaised, GetAlarm, CSV export over
  dense journal ids), `FB_TcEventBase` (entry/class compares,
  synchronous class-name/text requests), `FB_TcArguments`
  (typed arg accumulation), `FB_TcSourceInfo`, reduced
  `FB_TcCauseRemedy`/`FB_TcDetail`.  METHOD calls become
  edge-triggered `nCmd` inputs, event classes are UDINT ids,
  async text-request/remote-logger families documented as
  reduced.  Ctest `tc3_eventlog_io`.
- **Integration:** Event service exists in TetherPLC (raise/query); needs severity/category model parity.

**Description:** The function block checks which IPC diagnostic parameters are available and creates a register for this purpose. Specifically, a list of all available parameter modules is created. The function block only needs to determine this once, typically at the start of the program. If diagnostic parameters of a remote system are to be queried by means of a non-local AMS Net Id, the function block must be executed after its start.

### Tc3_JsonXml — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_JsonXml_EN`

- **Category:** Standard · **Tier:** T1
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_JsonXml_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 322
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED (JSON SAX core, nested, pretty writer,
  JSON DOM, reduced XML DOM)** —
  `compat/tc3/tc3_jsonxml.st`: `FB_JsonSaxWriter` (Begin/AddString/
  AddInt/AddReal/AddBool/AddNull/End/Clear plus ObjBegin/ArrBegin/
  EndAny on a 16-level container stack; `"`/`\` escaping),
  `FB_JsonSaxReader` (Load + GetString/GetInt/GetReal/GetBool by
  dotted path — objects via member names, arrays via numeric
  indices; container values return raw JSON text), `FB_JsonWriter`/
  `FB_JsonReader` aliases, `FB_JsonSaxPrettyWriter`/`FB_JsonPrettyWriter`
  (same command set + SetIndent, newline+space indentation; no
  compact-array mode), `FB_JsonDomParser`/`FB_JsonDom` — a
  fixed-table JSON DOM (48 nodes): iterative descent Load,
  Clear, Root, Child (0-based), ChildByName, ChildCount,
  NodeType, NodeKey, NodeText, ToJson, AppendObject/Array/
  String/Int/Real/Bool/Null; `bError`/`nErrId` on malformed
  input — and `FB_XmlDomParser`/`FB_XmlDom` — a
  fixed-table DOM (48 nodes, depth 16, 4 attrs/node, names ≤31,
  text/attr ≤127, output ≤511): Load-from-string, Clear, Root,
  Child (0-based), ChildByName, ChildCount, NodeName, NodeText,
  NodeXml, AttrCount, AttrByName, ToXml, AppendChild,
  AppendAttribute, AppendText; `bError`/`nErrId` on malformed
  input.  Documented reductions: no JSON DynDom/
  ReadWriteDataType, no DOM iterators/events, no XML
  iterators/namespaces/entities/
  CDATA/comments, no file persistence, 3-decimal REAL printing,
  255/1023-char documents, `.`-separated path keys.
  Ctest `tc3_jsonxml_io` (JSON + XML + pretty + DOM consumers).
- **Integration:** JSON/XML codecs are pure (T0); file persistence needs a filesystem service.

### Tc2_Drive — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_Drive_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/Drive · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_Drive_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 26
- **Status: PARTIAL** — `compat/tc2/tc2_drive.st` implements the general SoE surface over a new `tplc-soe` service (`ec.soe.slave`/`ec.soe.state`/`ec.soe.cmd` Tether IO params on `tether_io_motion_server`, deterministic per-slave simulation): `FB_SoEReset`, `FB_SoEWritePassword`, `FB_SoEExecuteCommand`, `FB_SoEWriteCommandControl`, `FB_SoEReadCommandState`, `FB_SoEReadDiagMessage`, `FB_SoEReadDiagNumber`, `FB_SoEReadDiagNumberList`, `FB_SoEReadClassXDiag`, `FB_SoEReadAmplifierTemperature`, `FB_SoEReadMotorTemperature`, `FB_SoEReadDcBusVoltage`, `FB_SoEReadDcBusCurrent`, plus `FB_SoEReadStatus` (S-0-0135 readback used by the conversion functions), the AX5000 blocks (`FB_SoEAX5000ReadActMainVoltage`, `FB_SoEAX5000SetMotorCtrlWord`, `FB_SoEAX5000FirmwareUpdate`, `FB_SoEAX5000ParkAxis`) and the four SimplePlcMotion blocks (`FB_CoEDriveEnable`, `FB_CoEDriveMoveVelocity`, `FB_SoEDriveEnable`, `FB_SoEDriveMoveVelocity` over `FB_MotionAxis`). e2e `tc2_drive_io` (mask `0x3fff`, 14 checks). Not covered: `ST_DriveRef`/`_ByDriveRef` naming (flattened `Drive : UDINT` port address instead), `F_ConvWordToSTAX5000C1D`/`F_ConvWordToSTAX5000DriveStatus`/`F_ConvWordToSTIndraDriveCsC1D`/`F_ConvWordToSTIndraDriveCsDriveStatus`/`F_GetVersionTcDrive` (TwinCAT STRUCT returns the dialect cannot model; raw status/class-1 words are on the read FBs), real SoE mailbox timing/profiles (simulated command state only), firmware flashing.
- **Integration:** Drive-specific function blocks: axis backend + CiA-402-style drive profiles (Tether DS402 work is directly relevant).

### Tc3_DriveMotionControl — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_DriveMotionControl_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/Drive · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_DriveMotionControl_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 14
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED** — the 14 entries are the single-axis MC set
  already provided by `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2.st` (the dialect has no
  library namespaces, so the Tc3 library shares the Tc2_MC2 FB
  implementations rather than duplicating them): MC_Power, MC_Reset,
  MC_SetPosition, MC_Home, MC_Jog, MC_Halt, MC_MoveAbsolute,
  MC_MoveModulo, MC_MoveRelative, MC_MoveVelocity, MC_Stop,
  MC_TouchProbe, MC_AbortTrigger, AXIS_REF (UDINT handle).
  `MC_AbortTrigger` cancels an armed probe through manufacturer
  object `0x2001` (probe abort request) on both motion backends —
  in-process `MotionService` axis state, over Tether IO the
  `mc.<slave>.2001` param backed by `SimulatedCiA402Drive`.
  e2e `tc2_mc2_probe`/`tc2_mc2_probe_io` (mask `0x3ff`). Remaining
  gaps are the shared MC-model ones (int32 user units, no hardware
  latch, per-axis not per-trigger abort), not Tc3-specific APIs.
- **Integration:** Drive motion control: axis backend + drive profiles.

#### Organization blocks › Touch probe

##### `MC_AbortTrigger` — §5.2.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Execute` | `BOOL` | The command is executed with the rising edge and the |

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Done` | `BOOL` | TRUE as soon as the touch probe cycle has been |

**Description:** The function block MC_AbortTrigger cancels a touch probe cycle started by MC_TouchProbe. MC_TouchProbe starts a touch probe cycle by activating a position latch in the drive hardware. The function block MC_AbortTrigger can be used to terminate the procedure before the trigger signal has activated the position latch. If the touch probe cycle has completed successfully, it is not necessary to call up this function block.

The position is captured via an external hardware latch and is therefore highly accurate and independent of the cycle time. The function block controls this mechanism and determines the externally recorded position.

### Tc2_MC2_Drive — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_MC2_Drive_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_MC2_Drive_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 41
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED** — `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2_drive.st` provides all
  41 APIs (e2e `tc2_mc2_drive_io`, mask `0xfffffff`, 28 checks over
  `tether_io_motion_server --clock sim`; the OD objects are also
  served by the in-process `MotionService`).
  Beckhoff-general and CoE blocks drive `FB_MotionAxis` OP4/OP5; the
  SoE set drives `FB_Soe` with `slave = Axis - 1`. State with no
  DS402 object uses manufacturer-specific sim objects `0x2002`
  (position offset), `0x2003` (brake command), `0x2004` (park
  command), `0x2005` (CoE command) and `0x2006..0x2009` (flying-saw
  characteristics), exposed as `mc.<slave>.<idx>` params on Tether
  IO and as `MotionService` axis fields in-process. `AXIS_REF` is
  the UDINT handle. Documented simplifications: the sim objects
  record commands/values only (no physical brake/park/offset/saw
  behavior); `FB_SoERead`/`FB_SoEWrite` cover only the S-0-0135
  status word and S-0-0267 password elements (arbitrary P-0-xxxx
  access reports Error); `MC_FlyingSawCharacValues` flattens to
  `Value0..Value3`; `FB_CoEAX8000BrakeTest.Succeeded` reports
  command acceptance (no torque verification); positions stay int32
  user units (no LREAL engineering-unit model).
- **Integration:** MC function blocks for drives: axis backend + drive profile handling.

#### Function blocks › General CoE

##### `FB_CoERead` — §4.3.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cancelled.*)` | `` | — |
| `NetId` | `T_AmsNetID` | String which contains the AMS Network ID of the PC |

**VAR_IN_OUT / Inputs-Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Axis` | `AXIS_REF` | — |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Busy` | `BOOL` | This output is set when the function block is activated, |

**Description:** The function block FB_CoERead allows data to be read from an object directory of an EtherCAT slave through an SDO (Service Data Object) access. This requires the slave to have a mailbox and to support the CoE (CANopen over EtherCAT) protocol. With the help of the SubIndex and Index parameters a selection is made as to which object should be read out. Via CompleteAccess := TRUE the parameter can be read with sub-elements.

##### `FB_CoEWrite` — §4.3.2

| Parameter | Type | Description |

| `SubIndex` | `BYTE;(*CoE sub index*)` | — |
| `pSrcBuf` | `PVOID;(*Contains the address of the buffer containing the data to be send*)` | — |
| `BufLen` | `UDINT;(*Contains the max. number of bytes to be received*)` | — |
| `Execute` | `BOOL;(*Function block execution is triggered by a rising edge at this input.*)` | — |
| `Timeout` | `TIME := DEFAULT_ADS_TIMEOUT` | — |
| `CompleteAccess` | `BOOL;(*Function block reads the complete object with all sub index*)` | — |

**VAR_IN_OUT / Inputs-Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Axis` | `AXIS_REF` | — |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Busy` | `BOOL` | This output is set when the function block is activated, |

**Description:** With the function block FB_CoEWrite, an object from the object directory of an EtherCAT slave can be written via an SDO (Service Data Object) download. This requires the slave to have a mailbox and to support the CoE (CANopen over EtherCAT) protocol. With the help of the SubIndex and Index parameters a selection is made as to which object should be written. Via CompleteAccess := TRUE the parameter can be written with sub-elements.

### Tc2_MC2_FlyingSaw — `TF5055_TC3_NC_Flying_Saw_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5055_TC3_NC_Flying_Saw_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 3
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED (simplified coupling)** — all three FBs live
  in `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2_drive.st` and are covered by the
  `tc2_mc2_drive_io` e2e (mask `0xfffffff`): `MC_GearInVelo`
  (velocity-ratio PV coupling, 0x606C -> 0x60FF),
  `MC_GearInPos` (position-ratio CSP coupling, 0x6064 -> 0x607A),
  `MC_ReadFlyingSawCharacteristics` (OD 0x2006..0x2009 ->
  `Value0..Value3`, the `MC_FlyingSawCharacValues` STRUCT flattened).
  Not modeled: the Universal Flying Saw sync-point cam evaluation —
  `MC_GearInPos` has no `CamTableCharac` input and does not compute
  the exact synchronous point/velocity of the real block; the
  characteristic values are stored/read but not consumed by the
  coupling.
- **Integration:** Flying saw: specialized motion kernel on the axis backend.

### Tc2_MC2_XFC+Tc2_NciXFC+AdvancedHoming_XFC — `TF5065_TC3_Motion_Control_XFC_XFC_NCI_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5065_TC3_Motion_Control_XFC_XFC_NCI_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 30
- **Status:** PARTIAL — kinematic/DC-time/cam/switch/touch-probe subset in `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2_xfc.st` (`tc2_mc2_xfc` ctest, mask `0xffff`); EL-terminal, NciXFC path and AdvancedHoming blocks pending
- **Integration:** XFC/NCI extensions + advanced homing: NC kernel features. Implemented subset uses `FB_MotionAxis` OP6 snapshots + per-FB TON scan clocks (T_DCTIME32 = low32 of ns clock, ~4.29 s wrap; linear extrapolation only, no profile evaluation). Not covered: `XFC_EL1258_TouchProbe`, `XFC_EL2212/EL2258/EL2262_MultiEdge`, `XFC_*PathPosition*`/`XFC_Path*Cam`/`MC_PathDigitalCamSwitch_MultiEdge` (NCI path kernel), all AdvancedHoming step/reference blocks; `CAMSWITCH_REF`/`TRACK_REF`/`OUTPUT_REF`/`XFC_TRIGGER_REF` flatten to BOOL/LREAL members.

### Tc2_NCI+Tc2_PlcInterpolation+Tc2_NC — `TF5100_TC3_NC_I_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5100_TC3_NC_I_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 103
- **Status: IMPLEMENTED** — compat/tc2/tc2_nci.st (NCI channel/FIFO/M-func/R-params/zero-shift; G-code owned by Tether) — ctest tc2_nci_io + tc2_nci_gcode_io.
### Tc2_NcDrive — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_NcDrive_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc2_NcDrive_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 21
- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED — all 20 SoE/CoE/AX5000 FBs covered by `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2_drive.st` (NCTOPLC_AXIS_REF/sNetId flatten to the same UDINT axis handle + NetId; e2e `tc2_mc2_drive_io`); `compat/tc2/tc2_ncdrive.st` adds `F_GetVersionTcNcDrive`
- **Integration:** NC drive function blocks: axis backend.

**Description:** The drive (S-0-0099) can be reset with the function block FB_SoEReset. In the case of multiple-channel devices if necessary, both channels will have to perform a reset. ### Tc2_NcFifoAxes — `TF5060_TCNC_FIFOAXES_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5060_TCNC_FIFOAXES_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 8
- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED — `compat/tc2/tc2_ncfifoaxes.st` wraps the `tplc-fifo` service + `FB_Fifo` builtin (4 channels x 8 axes x 1000 LREAL rows, 8-column fixed stride); `include/tplc/tplc_fifo.h` ABI, in-process `FifoService`, and `FifoIoService` over `fifo.*` params on `tether_io_motion_server` (rows consumed one per 1 ms of `mc.time` drive clock into `0x607A` CSP targets on the integrated CiA402 axes). e2e `tc2_ncfifoaxes` + `tc2_ncfifoaxes_io` green (integrate/dimension/write/override/start/drain/overwrite/disintegrate). Deviations: numeric setpoint FIFO (not the `nc.fifo` G-code block queue), override percent is recorded but does not rescale absolute rows, `iGroupPosition` is 1-based column index.
- **Integration:** FIFO axes (synchronous data streams): NC kernel + deterministic buffers.

### Tc2_NcKinematicTransformation — `TF5110-TF5113_TC3_Kinematic_Transformation_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5110-TF5113_TC3_Kinematic_Transformation_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 12
- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED — `compat/tc2/tc2_nckin.st` (all 12 APIs over the
  `tplc-kin` service / `FB_Kin` builtin; Tether `kinematics::ForwardKinematics`
  engine on both backends) — ctest `tc2_nckin` + `tc2_nckin_io`.
  Deviations: `oidTrafo` is the object index 0..7 (TwinCAT binds the object
  via the project); `ST_KinAxes`/`NCTOPLC_NCICHANNEL_REF`/`U_KinMetaInfo`/
  `E_KINSTATUS` flatten to arrays + scalars; pointer-based `FB_KinCalcMultiTrafo`
  carries one object's LREAL vector per call; the two FUNCTIONs with output
  params are FUNCTION_BLOCKs; backward IK is position-only damped least
  squares (orientation unconstrained, seed joints in input slots 4+).
- **Integration:** Kinematic transformations (robot-like chains): kinematics engine on the axis backend.

### Tc3_MC2_AdvancedHoming — `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_MC2_AdvancedHoming_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/NC2 · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TwinCAT_3_PLC_Lib_Tc3_MC2_AdvancedHoming_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 16
- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED — `compat/tc3/tc3_mc2_ah.st` (all 16 APIs over a
  shared `AH_Run` engine on `FB_MotionAxis`: PV-mode searches, switch-edge/
  velocity-undershoot detection, position assign via 0x6064) — ctest
  `tc3_mc2_ah` + `tc3_mc2_ah_io` (mask `0xffff`, 16 checks).
  Deviations: `MC_HomingParameter`/`MC_Ref_Signal_Ref`/enums flatten to
  scalar/BOOL/LREAL members; reference signals are caller-supplied BOOLs
  (the sim has no physical switch/encoder input, tests derive them from
  position); block/lag detection uses velocity undershoot vs
  `DetectionVelocityLimit`/`LagLimit`, not torque/lag telemetry;
  `BufferMode`, `OptDisableDriveAccess`, drive-parameter backup and
  `MC_HomingParameterDrive` torque fields are accepted but not modeled.
- **Integration:** Advanced homing routines: axis backend homing state machines.

**Description:** The function block MC_MoveAbsoluteCA instructs a single axis to move to the absolute position defined in the function block, based on Collision Avoidance. Collision Avoidance has higher priority than the motion command. Therefore, the axis may slow down or wait while the motion command is executed to avoid a collision. The function block does not output the signal Done until the axis has reached its target position.

**Description:** This function block resets all motion object-related errors and transitions the motion object out of state ErrorStop. The resulting state is Disabled, if no Enable is requested for the motion object (e.g. via MC_Power). It results in DiscreteMotion, if the motion object has a closed control loop and a controlled error reaction is still ongoing. Otherwise, Standstill is the resulting state. This function block does not affect the output of motion function block instances.

While the axis is in state Stopping, no other function block can perform any motion on the same axis. The Done output is set immediately after zero dynamics is reached. #### PLC libraries › Tc3_Mc3Ptp › Function Blocks › Synchronized Motion

##### `MC_GearIn` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §5.3.5.10.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Master` | `Type_Master1D [} 230]` | Reference to the master axis |
| `Slave` | `Reference To AXIS_REF [} 307]` | Reference to the slave axis |
| `Execute` | `BOOL` | Trigger the command with rising edge. |
| `r` | `synchronous, the slave's velocity, acceleration and position changes are (RatioNumerator / RatioDenominator) times the master's values. A negative value moves the slave opposite to the` | — |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `InGear` | `BOOL` | TRUE once the slave has reached the master's velocity and |

**Description:** Synchronizes the slave onto the master's velocity and acceleration scaled by a constant gear ratio. Synchronizes as fast as the function block's inputs Acceleration, Deceleration and Jerk allow. MC_GearIn has no input Velocity. The axis' parameter Maximum Velocity is used while synchronizing. Once the slave has reached the scaled velocity and acceleration, the function block's output InGear signals true and the slave is coupled to the scaled master. From then on the slave's dynamics and position are coupled to the scaled master's, ignoring any dynamic restrictions (commanded dynamics as well as axis parameters). The position relationship when reaching InGear is consequently not configurable. Use MC_GearInPos when a specific position relationship is required. The command may be ended by sending another command. Using input BufferMode := Aborting makes the next command take over immediately while input BufferMode := Buffered queues the next command. It will then take over as soon as InGear is reached.

##### `MC_GearInPos` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §5.3.5.10.2

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `Master` | `Type_Master1D [} 230]` | Reference to the master axis |
| `Slave` | `Reference To AXIS_REF [} 307]` | Reference to the slave axis |
| `Execute` | `BOOL` | Trigger the command with rising edge. |
| `r` | `synchronous the slave's velocity, acceleration and position changes are (RatioNumerator / RatioDenominator) times the master's. A negative value` | — |

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `InSync` | `BOOL` | TRUE once the output SyncState reaches value InSync: the |

**Description:** Synchronizes the slave onto the master's velocity and acceleration scaled by a constant gear ratio, anchoring at slave position = SlaveSyncPosition + (RatioNumerator / RatioDenominator) * (master position - MasterSyncPosition). Synchronizes as fast as the function block's inputs Velocity, Acceleration, Deceleration and Jerk allow. Once the slave has reached the scaled velocity and acceleration as well as the position described above, the slave is coupled to the master. From then on any dynamic restrictions (commanded dynamics as well as axis parameters) are ignored. If it is not necessary to configure the position relationship in advance, use MC_GearIn instead. Synchronicity is reached as early as possible and is thus independent of whether commanded synchronous positions have been reached by either master or slave. The outputs InSync and SyncState provide detailed information on the progress of synchronization. The direction in which the slave may move while synchronizing can be restricted via the input AllowedSlaveSyncDirections. The command may be ended by sending another command. Using input BufferMode := Aborting for the next command makes it take over immediately while input BufferMode := Buffered for the next command queues it. It will then take over as soon as output SyncState reaches InSync.

**Description:** This function block adds a cam table coupling on a slave. Generated setpoints from single cam table couplings are internally added. As MC_CamIn, this function block can also be used to initiate camming-based synchronization. As this function block is used for multi-camming, some special rules apply: The same master can be used in multiple cam table couplings. A cam table can only be used once in a slave.

The cam table coupling that should be removed has to be active when this function block is executed and the activation condition is met, otherwise an error is triggered. **Description:** This function block initiates camming-based synchronization on a slave. If the slave is already coupled to one or more cam table couplings, it switches to the cam table coupling that is entered in this function block. Note: Use MC_CamAdd to switch from single-camming to multi-camming. Switch back and forth between single-camming and multi-camming is possible and not limited.

| Parameter | Type | Description |

| `Done` | `BOOL` | Removal succeeded |
| `Busy` | `BOOL` | Function block is not finished and new output values are to be |

**Description:** This function block removes a cam table coupling from a slave. As a cam table can only be used once in a coupled slave, the master information is not needed. However, the cam table must be in use when this function block is executed and when the activation condition is met, otherwise an error is triggered. If there is no active coupling left and there are no pending commands to add couplings, the camming synchronization ends by itself and axis state changes to Standstill.

- **Integration:** Planar motion (XY/Gantry): multi-axis interpolation on the axis backend.

### Tc2_CncPlcopenP4 — `TF5200_JOBMANAGER_EN`

- **Category:** Motion/CNC · **Tier:** T4
- **Manual:** `TF5200_JOBMANAGER_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 1
- **Status:** DEFERRED — single entry MCV_GrpReadJobAck evaluates MC_MovePath job acknowledgements; needs the coordinated-motion trajectory engine (row 24 remainder)
- **Integration:** PLCopen P4 (packaging): state machines are T0 logic; full conformance needs the motion/packaging backends.

#### PLCopen function blocks

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `JobState` | `MCV_JOB_STATE                    Job information` | — |

**Description:** The function block is used to evaluate the end or abort operations of jobs commanded by an MC_MovePath [} 27] . The instance of the MC_MovePath [} 27] whose job acknowledgements are evaluated is identified via the “Fb” input.

### Tc2_Hydraulics — `TF5810_TC3_Hydraulic_Positioning_EN`

- **Category:** Motion · **Tier:** T3
- **Manual:** `TF5810_TC3_Hydraulic_Positioning_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 118
- **Status:** the standard PLCopen `MC_*_BkPlcMc` blocks (power/read/write/cam/gear/halt/jog/home/stop/table-select, ~75 entries) are covered by `compat/tc2/tc2_mc2.st` — ctest tc2_mc2_*_io. Remaining: the hydraulic drive-model FBs — `MC_AxCtrl*` (pressure/force/PI/de-stall control), `MC_AxRt*` (runtime axis: force/pressure/encoder actuals, hybrid axis, function generators), `MC_AxTable*` (cam-table file I/O), `MC_AxRuntime` — need a hydraulic axis model in Tether motion; on request. Status stands: hydraulic drive-model subset deferred pending a hydraulic axis model in Tether motion
- **Integration:** Hydraulic positioning: axis backend with hydraulic drive model.

### PfwLib_Processing — `TF8540_Plastic_Processing_Framework_EN`

- **Category:** Industry · **Tier:** T0
- **Manual:** `TF8540_Plastic_Processing_Framework_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 26
- **Status:** TcTvA alarm-visualization family delivered as `compat/tc2/tc2_pfwlib.st` (`FB_TcTvAMsgQueue`, 32-slot fixed table standing in for the POINTER TO `ST_TcTvA_Alarm_Itf` array) — ctest tc2_pfwlib_io. Remaining: temp-controller/force-control/process FBs (`FB_TempCtrl*`, `FB_FcMainBody`, `FB_PowerMeasurement`, `FB_TempParamSave/Load`, `FB_xL3403`, `FB_TempCtrlAdaptFm33xx`, `FB_TermCoe*/TermReg*`, `FB_ClockTimer*`) — machine-specific control algorithms, on request.
- **Integration:** Plastic-processing application library: process-control logic over image IO; machine specifics via fieldbus.

**Description:** This scenario example illustrates the PLC Expert Mode for a Message Logger in the PLC. In the sample program the function blocks of the TwinCAT Database Server are used to create a function block, which provides various methods for generating and reading messages. The database in which the messages are stored is created from the PLC. A sample application of the created function block is implemented in the MAIN program. A new database file is created every 7 days. Three different messages can be sent. In addition it is possible to call up the last message or all messages from a particular interval.

**Description:** This function block (actively) establishes a network connection to the third-party system. If successful, the internal parameters of the hLink variable are initialised. The same instance of the hLink variable must then be transferred to the other instances of the communication blocks FB_NLinkFetch [} 22], FB_NLinkWrite [} 24] or FB_NLinkClose [} 21]. In a PLC application one instance of this variables is required for each network connection (TwinCAT system<->Ethernet LAN adapter<->external controller).

### Tc3_Acsi+iec61850 family — `TF6510_TC3_IEC61850_EN`

- **Category:** Connectivity · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TF6510_TC3_IEC61850_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 485
- **Status:** MMS client core delivered in `compat/tc2/tc2_iec61850.st` + `tplc-iec61850` host service (libiec61850): connect/associate, read/write with FC suffixes, GetNameList, disconnect, status — e2e `tc2_iec61850_io` green against `tests/compat/iec61850_ied_fake`. RCB tranche delivered: `FB_Iec61850RCBGet`/`FB_Iec61850RCBSet`/`FB_Iec61850ReportPoll` (URCB `$RP$` + BRCB `$BR$` refs, rptEna/resv/resvTms/GI/PurgeBuf flags with server-state-aware write masks, dchg+GI InformationReport reception) — e2e `tc2_iec61850_rcb_io` (0x1ff) and `tc2_iec61850_brcb_io` (0x1ff incl. unsolicited IntgPd integrity report) green. Control tranche delivered: `FB_Iec61850ControlCmd` (select/selectWithValue/operate/cancel) + `FB_Iec61850ControlPoll` — ASY1-style CommandTermination events (invokeId/success/err/type/ctlNum/pending) over libiec61850 ControlObjectClient, fake `SWI1` BSC (SBO normal + cancel) verified incl. operate-before-select rejection, e2e `tc2_iec61850_ctl_io` green. GetRCBValues now covers the full libiec61850 attribute set (rptId/dataSet/confRev/bufTm/intgPd/sqNum/optFlds/trgOps/rptEna/resv/buffered/gi/purgeBuf/resvTms/entryId) via `FB_Iec61850RCBGet` outputs GI/PurgeBuf/ResvTms/EntryId. Data-set tranche delivered: `FB_Iec61850DataSetRead` (MMS ReadDataSet, "FCDA=value" lines) + `FB_Iec61850DataSetDirectory` (GetDataSetDirectory FCDA list) + `FB_Iec61850DataSetWrite` (WriteDataSetValues; member types taken from a fresh ReadDataSet, per-member access results checked) + `FB_Iec61850DataSetCreate`/`FB_Iec61850DataSetDelete` (DefineNamedVariableList/DeleteNamedVariableList; association-specific `@name` sets verified end to end) — e2e `tc2_iec61850_ds_io` green incl. write+read-back and create→directory→delete→gone. APC tranche delivered: structured ctlVal via libiec61850's simplified AnalogueValue path (scalar text -> wrapped setpoint structure) verified on fake `APC1` (CDC_APC, SBO normal + cancel) with mxVal.f read-back, e2e `tc2_iec61850_ctl_io` extended (mask 0xffff). Remaining depth: user-defined structured ctlVal member lists, GOOSE/SMV (blocked: AF_PACKET needs CAP_NET_RAW).
- **Integration:** IEC 61850/ACSI substation protocols: socket/MMS stack; large implementation.

#### Technical introduction

##### `General Client - Project structure` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §4.4

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fbConnection` | `FB_iec61850ClientClass` | — |
| `fbAdapter` | `FB_GseAdapterClass := (ipLinkStatus:=THIS^)` | — |

**Description:** Each of the client sample projects follows a general structure, which this document aims to explain. This structure includes the nesting of the function blocks in the Solution Explorer and the structure of the state machine in the client function block, which establishes the connection to the server and implements the data exchange. The basic structure of the TwinCAT IEC 61850 sample projects is based on the PLC project structure automatically generated by the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator. The TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator in turn uses the "TwinCAT XAE Project (XML format)" as a template when generating the solution. The data models communicated in the samples reflect different IEC 61850 servers. They differ from sample to sample and are enclosed with the source code as icd files. The ICD files can also be used by third-party software for the simulation of a server.

##### `General Server - Project structure` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §4.5

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fbConnection` | `FB_iec61850ConnectionClass := (ipAbortInd:=THIS^, ipAssociateInd:=THIS^, ipRe` | — |
| `leaseInd` | `=THIS^)` | — |
| `fbAdapter` | `FB_GseAdapterClass := (ipLinkStatus:=THIS^)` | — |
| `ipAdapter` | `I_GseAdapterClass` | — |
| `eStatus` | `E_GseLinkStatus` | — |

**Description:** All sample Server projects also follow a general structure, similar to the sample Client projects. In contrast to the client, the connection at the server is not actively established on the server side. After the program start, the server waits for a connection request from a client and accepts or rejects it. In addition, it must be possible for the server to establish connections to multiple clients.

**Description:** The natural byte order of the data on a TwinCAT system is referred to as the host byte order. The byte order of the data transmitted over the network is referred to as the network byte order. The network byte order of IEC 61850 data largely corresponds to the big-endian format, while the TwinCAT system uses the byte order of the little-endian format. This function block implements methods that allow the byte order of the IEC 61850 data to be changed (little-endian <-> big-endian).

##### `FB_GseSvFunctionGeneratorClass` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §6.3.3.6.8

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bValid` | `BOOL` | This output is TRUE if the signal generator configuration is valid, and FALSE if |

**Description:** This function block implements a simple sine function test signal generator. The generated sample values can be used to simulate SV communication.

#### PLC API › Function blocks › Communication › Sampled Values › FB_GseSvFunctionGeneratorClass

##### `Call` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.8.1

**Description:** The method generates a new signal sample. In signal sampling mode: ’SecondsPerSample‘, this method is called nOversampleFactor times in each PLC task cycle.

##### `Config` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.8.2

**Description:** This method configures the function generator based on the selected signal sampling mode (eMode), the PLC cycle time, the PLC cycle time correction factor (fCycleTimeCorrectionFactor), the configured oversampling factor (nOversampleFactor), the configured sampling rate (nSpecifiedSmpRate), and the signal frequency (fFrequency). The Config method is automatically called internally whenever these configuration parameters are changed.

##### `Reset` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.8.3

**Description:** The method resets the initial value, fSignal, to 0.0 and the sample number, nSample, to 0. After this method call, the next call to the method generates the first sample value with the number 0 again. If the configuration parameters are changed, the reset method is automatically called internally by the config method.

**Description:** This function block implements 8 test signal function generators according to the “PhsMeas1” data set of the UCA 61850-9-2LE (Light Edition). This function block can be used to generate simulation values for phases A, B, C, and N (up to 4 currents and 4 voltage values) for an SV communication test.

#### PLC API › Function blocks › Communication › Sampled Values › FB_GseSvPhsMeasGeneratorClass

##### `Call` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.9.1

**Description:** The method generates 4 new current samples (phases A, B, C, and N) and 4 new voltage samples (phases A, B, C, and N). In signal sampling mode: ’SecondsPerSample‘, this method is called nOversampleFactor times in each PLC task cycle.

##### `Config` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.9.2

**Description:** The method configures all 8 test signal function generators based on the selected signal sampling mode (eMode), the PLC task cycle time, the PLC cycle time correction factor (fCycleTimeCorrectionFactor), the configured oversampling factor (nOversampleFactor), the configured sampling rate (nSpecifiedSmpRate), and the signal frequency (fFrequency).

##### `Reset` (METHOD) — §6.3.3.6.9.3

**Description:** For all test signal function generators, this method resets the output value fSignal to 0.0 and the sample number nSample to 0. After this method call, the next call to the method generates the first sample value with the number 0 again. If the configuration parameters are changed, the reset method is automatically called internally by the config method.

#### PLC API › Function blocks

##### `FB_AsyncServiceResultClass` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §6.3.4

**Description:** The function block FB_AsyncServiceResultClass implements the I_AsyncServiceResultClass [} 463] interface for status query and tracking of asynchronous processes. The methods of the communication function block FB_iec61850CommonClass [} 247] for establishing/disconnecting the connection and activation of the IEC 61850 services return the interface pointer of type I_AsyncServiceResultClass [} 463] as parameter. The application can use this pointer to monitor and query the status/progress of service execution.

##### `FB_ServiceErrorClass` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §6.3.5

**Description:** The function block FB_ServiceErrorClass implements the I_ServiceErrorClass [} 468] interface for error query and storage. The methods of the object instances of the TwinCAT IEC 61850 data model and some services for establishing/disconnecting the connection return the interface pointer of type I_ServiceErrorClass [} 468] in the event of an error. This pointer can be used to perform a more detailed error analysis.

**Description:** This method grants authentication access.

##### `GetVerifyResult` (METHOD) → `BOOL` — §6.5.3.10.2

**VAR_OUTPUT / Outputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bAccepted` | `BOOL` | — |
| `eType` | `E_AcseAuthentication` | — |
| `sMechanismName` | `STRING` | — |
| `sPassword` | `STRING` | — |
| `sRespondingPass` | `STRING` | — |
| `eResult` | `E_ACSE_AareResult` | — |
| `eDiagnostic` | `E_ACSE_AareDiagnostic` | — |
| `eAbrtDiagnostic` | `E_ACSE_AbrtDiagnostic` | — |

**Description:** This method provides a detailed result of the verification of the authentication data. The internal standard verification takes place on the server when the associate request data is received (AARQ telegram) and on the client when the associate response data is received (AARE telegram). With the GetVerifyResult return parameter value TRUE, the IEC 61850 server or client application may check or change the authentication status itself at a certain point in time, but only if authentication (authentication-functional-unit) has been activated in the communication requests of both communication partners.

##### `Reject` (METHOD) → `BOOL` — §6.5.3.10.3

**Return type:** `BOOL`

**Description:** This method denies authentication access.

##### `Verify` (METHOD) → `BOOL` — §6.5.3.10.4

**Return type:** `BOOL`

**Description:** This method performs the internal verification of the authentication parameters again.

##### `General Client - Project structure` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §7.1

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

**Description:** Each of the client sample projects follows a general structure, which this document aims to explain. This structure includes the nesting of the function blocks in the Solution Explorer and the structure of the state machine in the client function block, which establishes the connection to the server and implements the data exchange. The basic structure of the TwinCAT IEC 61850 sample projects is based on the PLC project structure automatically generated by the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator. The TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator in turn uses the "TwinCAT XAE Project (XML format)" as a template when generating the solution. The data models communicated in the samples reflect different IEC 61850 servers. They differ from sample to sample and are enclosed with the source code as icd files. The ICD files can also be used by third-party software for the simulation of a server.

##### `Client - GOOSE Subscriber (without Client-Server` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §7.12

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fbAdapter` | `FB_GseAdapterClass := (ipLinkStatus:=THIS^)` | — |
| `ipAdapter` | `I_GseAdapterClass` | — |
| `eStatus` | `E_GseLinkStatus` | — |

**Description:** In a Client project, the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator also generates a Client block by default (see: "General Client project structure" [} 664]). The Client block can then be used, for example, to activate/ deactivate the GOOSE Publisher on the Server side via Client-Server services such as "GetGoCBDataValues" or "SetGoCBDataValues" or to configure the GoCBs. In some cases, however, Client-Server communication with the device should be dispensed with and only a "pure" GOOSE Subscriber implemented. Such a Subscriber can automatically start receiving GOOSE messages after the PLC program start. This example shows the implementation of a Subscriber, but without the Client-Server communication part. The parts of the Client project that are not needed have been deliberately removed in this example.

##### `General Server - Project structure` (FUNCTION_BLOCK) — §7.15

**Description:** All sample Server projects also follow a general structure, similar to the sample Client projects. In contrast to the client, the connection at the server is not actively established on the server side. After the program start, the server waits for a connection request from a client and accepts or rejects it. In addition, it must be possible for the server to establish connections to multiple clients.

**Description:** In a Server project, the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator also generates a Server block and one or more instances of the Server session block by default (see: "General Server project structure" [} 700]). The Server and ServerSession block can, for example, ensure that the Publisher can be activated/deactivated from the Client via Client-Server services such as "GetGoCBDataValues" or "SetGoCBDataValues" or that the GoCBs can be configured. In some cases, however, Client-Server communication with the device should be omitted and only a "pure" GOOSE Publisher should be implemented. Such a Publisher can automatically start sending GOOSE messages after the PLC program start. This example shows the implementation of a Publisher, but without the Client-Server communication part. The parts of the Server project that are not needed have been deliberately removed in this example.

The spontaneous time required by the server can be specified from an external source (e.g. from a GPS clock). Among other things, a current time is required when sending reports.

**Description:** This sample shows the Unbuffered Reporting implementation in a TwinCAT IEC61850 server project. The UrCBs (unbuffered report control blocks) and Datasets required for reporting can be configured in the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator or imported from an existing SCL file (e.g. ICD file). The instances of the UrCBs and the Datasets are created automatically during code generation (usually below LLN0). The initial values of the UrCB attributes can already be configured in the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator.

The instances of the BRCBs and the Datasets are created automatically during code generation (usually below LLN0). The initial values of the BRCB attributes can already be configured in the TwinCAT Telecontrol Configurator.

##### `TLS - Secure client-server communication using` (METHOD) — §7.28

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bEnable` | `BOOL` | — |
| `bPSK` | `BOOL` | — |

**Description:** This example shows how secure data communication can be implemented using TLS (Transport Layer Security) in a TwinCAT IEC 61850 client and server application. The TLS protocol only allows encryption of client-server communication. The GOOSE publisher/subscriber data cannot be encrypted in this way. If you are using an older version of the TwinCAT IEC 61850 Telecontrol Configurator, the TLS functionality may not be supported there yet. To compile and test this sample project without errors you need a newer version of the TF6510 IEC 61850 Telecontrol.

**Description:** This sample shows how a plain text password can be activated and configured to authenticate the connection in a TwinCAT IEC 61850 client or server application. This sample also shows how the server application can control the authentication process itself at runtime. This means that the application can accept or reject the connection depending on the password received. This sample also shows how the services and parameters supported by the IEC 61850 server are enabled and configured in the TwinCAT client and server application. The sample also shows how the server can control the negotiation of the supported services and parameters itself at runtime. The TwinCAT IEC 61850 server application can, for example, reject the services and/or parameters proposed by the client depending on the password received and thus restrict access to these services or parameters for certain connections or users. If you are using an older version of the TwinCAT IEC 61850 Telecontrol Configurator, the functionalities presented in this sample may not yet be supported. To be able to compile and test this sample without errors, you need a newer version of the TF6510 IEC 61850 Telecontrol.

- **Category:** Connectivity · **Tier:** T2

- **Status:** IMPLEMENTED (sim contract) — `tplc-ecsync` host service reads/writes the `ec.dc.*` params over Tether IO (`TPLC_EC_IO`, falls back to `TPLC_MOTION_IO`); `compat/tc3/tc3_ecsync.st` provides `FB_EcExtSyncExtTimes` (`sNetId` nonempty enables sync -> `bTS1Done`; empty disables) and `FB_EcExtSyncIsSynchronized` (`nSyncWindow` UDINT ns -> `bSynchronized`/`bNotConnected`) over the `FB_EcSync` builtin; `tc3_ecsync_io` e2e green against `tether_io_motion_server --clock sim` plus a no-endpoint not-connected replay. Remaining: real-master hookup needs DCManager/EtherCATDC stats bridged into the same params; the documented 10-cycle diff check is reduced to a per-call window compare; licensed TF6225 surface semantics beyond the two FBs.
- **Integration:** EtherCAT DC (distributed clocks) sync needs master sync hooks.

**Description:** This function block FB_EcExtSyncIsSynchronized checks whether the internal and external clocks are synchronized (bSynchronized). For this purpose, the system checks whether the difference between the clocks over 10 cycles is within the specified synchronization window nSyncWindow. ### Tc3_IotBase — `TF6701_TC3_IoT_Communication_MQTT_EN`

- **Category:** Connectivity · **Tier:** T2
- **Manual:** `TF6701_TC3_IoT_Communication_MQTT_EN.pdf` · **API entries:** 372
- **Status:** IoT function surface folded into `compat/tc2/tc2_mqtt.st` — ctest tc2_mqtt_io. Delivered: MQTT 3.1.1 client FBs (connect/disconnect/publish/subscribe/unsubscribe/receive/status), retained-message flag on delivery, client-side `F_MqttTopicMatch` wildcard matching, MQTT 3.1.1 last-will (topic/payload/QoS/retain on connect) plus `FB_IotMqttAbort` for ungraceful drop (socket shutdown without DISCONNECT so the broker fires the will), python fake-broker e2e incl. retained delivery, cross-connection broadcast, and will delivery. Message-queue tranche delivered: `FB_IotMqttMessage` (topic/payload/qos/msgid/retained members) + `FB_IotMqttMessageQueue` (level `Pump` drains one pending message per scan into a 16-entry ring, edge `DequeueReq`/`ResetReq`, `Queued` count, popped message on `Topic`/`Payload`/`QoS`/`MessageId`/`Retained` outputs) — e2e `tc2_mqtt_queue_io` green (pump → FIFO dequeue ×3 → reset → publish/dequeue → disconnect, mask 0x1ff). QoS2 tranche: fake broker now does real PUBREC/PUBREL/PUBCOMP both directions, per-filter granted QoS, multi-topic SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE; e2e covers subscribe@qos2 + publish@qos2 + dequeue reporting QoS=2 (mask 0x6ff). TLS tranche: paho rebuilt with `PAHO_WITH_SSL` (links `paho-mqtt3cs-static` + OpenSSL), `TplcMqttConnectCfg` gains use_tls/tls_insecure/tls_ca_file/tls_cert_file/tls_key_file, `FB_IotMqttClient` gains UseTls/TlsInsecure/TlsCaFile/TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile, fake broker `--tls` mode; e2e `tc2_mqtt_tls_io` green (insecure + CA-verified connections, mask 0x3ff). Broker-message-age tranche: `TplcMqttStatus.last_msg_age_ms` (repurposed reserved slot, struct still 48B) tracks ms since last inbound PUBLISH/connect; `FB_Mqtt` OP3 copies it to `LASTMSGSINCE`; new `FB_IotMqttStatus` FB exposes Connected/State/LastMsgId/LastError/TimeSinceLastBrokerMsgMs (GetTimeSinceLastBrokerMessage equivalent; transport pings not surfaced by the sync client) — covered in the TLS e2e (mask 0x7ff). Exponential-backoff tranche: `mqtt_backoff` vtable op + per-connection watchdog thread that re-issues CONNECT from an owned ConnectSpec with a doubling delay (min..max, reset on success); `FB_Mqtt` OP10 + `FB_IotMqttBackoff` (Enable edge, MinMs/MaxMs); `TplcMqttStatus.state` now reports live `MQTTClient_isConnected`; fake broker `--bounce <topic> <delay>` drops client conns on a trigger publish; e2e `tc2_mqtt_backoff_io` green (baseline echo -> bounce -> watchdog reconnect -> resubscribe -> second echo, mask 0x3ff). MQTT5 tranche: `TplcMqttConnectCfg` gains version + five connect properties (session expiry, receive max, topic alias max, request response/problem info); `FB_Mqtt` OP1 reads appended MQTTVER/M5* members; the service creates v5 clients via `MQTTClient_createWithOptions` (MQTTVERSION_5) + `MQTTClient_connect5` (cleanstart, not cleansession) and routes publish/subscribe/unsubscribe through the `*5` APIs per connection; new `FB_IotMqtt5Client` ST FB exposes the property inputs; fake broker parses v5 CONNECT properties/will properties and emits v5 CONNACK/SUBACK/PUBLISH/UNSUBACK framing; e2e `tc2_mqtt5_io` green (connect+props -> sub -> pub -> echo -> unsub -> disconnect, mask 0x3f). MQTT5 publish-properties tranche: `TplcMqtt5PubProps` + `mqtt_publish5` vtable op (payload format indicator, message expiry, content type, response topic, correlation data, user properties as a k=v;k=v list); `FB_Mqtt` OP11 + appended M5PUB* members; new `FB_IotMqtt5Publish` ST FB; fake broker decodes inbound v5 publish properties and logs them; e2e `tc2_mqtt5_io` verifies the full props publish echoes and the broker log shows ctype/user-props (mask 0xff). MQTT5 subscribe-properties tranche: `TplcMqtt5SubProps` + `mqtt_subscribe5` vtable op (no-local, retain-as-published, retain-handling 0/1/2, subscription identifier, user properties); `FB_Mqtt` OP12 + appended M5SUB* members; new `FB_IotMqtt5Subscribe` ST FB; fake broker decodes v5 SUBSCRIBE properties and per-topic option bits and logs them; e2e subscribes with sid=7 + user props and asserts the SUBPROPS log lines (mask 0xff). MQTT5 received-property tranche: `TplcMqttRx5` (base TplcMqttRx + payload format, message expiry, subscription id, content type, response topic, correlation data, user properties) + `mqtt_receive5` vtable op; `MqttService::receive5` extracts `msg->properties` via `MQTTProperties_getProperty(At)`; `FB_Mqtt` OP13 + appended M5RX* members; new `FB_IotMqtt5Receive` ST FB; fake broker now forwards the publisher's raw v5 property block to v5 subscribers; e2e verifies every property output round-trips (mask 0xff). MQTT5 message-queue tranche: `FB_IotMqtt5Message` (message record with the full PUBLISH property set as members) + `FB_IotMqtt5MessageQueue` (same level-Pump/edge-DequeueReq ring model as the v3 queue but draining via `FB_IotMqtt5Receive`, properties preserved per slot); e2e publishes a property-bearing message, pumps, dequeues and verifies expiry/content-type/correlation/user-properties (mask 0x1ff). MQTT5 request/response tranche: `FB_IotMqtt5RequestResponse` drives TwinCAT's Request/Response shape as a bounded state machine (subscribe response inbox -> publish with ResponseTopic + CorrelationData -> poll FB_IotMqtt5Receive for a topic+correlation match, TimeoutScans guard); fake broker `--responder <topic>` answers correlated requests with a 'pong' carrying the correlation property; e2e `tc2_mqtt5_req_io` green (mask 0x07). MQTT5 property-container tranche: all six §5.1.2.9 FBs exist in `compat/tc2/tc2_mqtt.st` — `FB_IotMqtt5ConnAckProperties`/`DisconnectProperties`/`PublishProperties`/`SubscribeProperties`/`UnsubscribeProperties` are member containers mirroring the property fields (this dialect has no REFERENCE TO parameters, so publish/subscribe take the same fields as direct inputs and the containers stage values for user code); `FB_IotMqtt5UserProperties` is a functional bounded list (edge AddReq appends a k=v pair, edge ClearReq resets, 8 pairs max, `k=v;k=v` on Encoded) exercised end to end in `tc2_mqtt5_io` — the case builds `k1=v1;k2=v2` dynamically and the broker-verified echo carries it (mask 0x1ff). Remaining depth: `OnMqtt5*`/`OnMqttMessage` callback-style delivery (needs an event mechanism beyond the synchronous scan model), HTTP egress (no HTTP FBs documented in Tc3_IotBase — covered by the socket-service integration note).
- **Integration:** IoT base: MQTT/HTTP egress via socket service.

##### `ActivateExponentialBackoff` (METHOD) — §5.1.1.1.6

**VAR_INPUT / Inputs**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tMqttBackoffMin TIME` | `Describes the initial delay value for the new connection attempt. Time` | — |
| `tMqttBackoffMax TIME` | `Describes the largest delay value. Once this value has been reached, all new` | — |
| `Time` | `connection attempts are made at these intervals.` | — |

**Description:** A feature referred to as "exponential backoff" can be used to avoid burdening the message broker with unnecessary connection requests in case of a connection error. In the event of a TLS connection error involving the message broker, the reconnect rate is adjusted multiplicatively. This function can be activated using the ActivateExponentialBackoff() [} 61] method. The parameters of the method specify the minimum and maximum time for the algorithm. The minimum time describes the initial delay value for the new connection attempt. The maximum time describes the highest delay value. The delay values are doubled until the maximum value is reached. Once a connection has been established, the backoff rate is reset to the original value. The DeactivateExponentialBackoff() [} 62] method can be used to deactivate this function programmatically.

##### `DeactivateExponentialBackoff` (METHOD) — §5.1.1.1.7

This function can be activated using the ActivateExponentialBackoff() [} 61] method. The parameters of the method specify the minimum and maximum time for the algorithm. The minimum time describes the initial delay value for the new connection attempt. The maximum time describes the highest delay value. The delay values are doubled until the maximum value is reached. Once a connection has been established, the backoff rate is reset to the original value. The DeactivateExponentialBackoff() [} 62] method can be used to deactivate this function programmatically.
